answer: Random mutual audit stops fake identities. Two strangers audit each agent to check whether one operator hides behind several accounts. Auditors stake a deposit: a missed fake forfeits it, a catch earns part of the fine. One failure removes the mesa of accounts; the deposit, hard as basalt, is burned, so a ledge of claims cannot stand. Making 100 fakes costs 100 deposits and 200 audits; an honest agent pays once and keeps undiluted rewards.
